name: exclude-the-wrong-voice
style: 1997 New York East Coast boom bap rap, 90 BPM, sparse minor-key loop with an eerie bent guitar stab, hard dusty kick and cracking snare, turntable-cut spoken number count before each rule. Heavyset Brooklyn man on the mic, deep plummy chest voice with a slight wheeze, unhurried conversational flow lagging behind the beat, calm menace, dry vocal right up front
exclude: gravelly old man voice, female vocals, high youthful voice, radio announcer, orchestral strings, spoken word poetry, trap hi-hats, 808 rolls, lo-fi chill, autotune, sung chorus, big reverb
lyrics:
[Intro]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Scratch: count]
[Verse]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Scratch: count]
[Verse]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Scratch: count]
[Verse]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.
